entries.title: Victoria of Many Faces
entries.jpTitle: 手札が多めのビクトリア

review.en:
Episode #9: No Matter What Happens From Here

"It was wonderful right to the very end. Once again, it felt like watching a beautiful classic film. Nonna... you really stole the show. (sobbing)"

Even the finale felt like an entire classic film in itself—especially an old European one, perhaps.

The revelation about Jeffrey and his brother's past was quite unexpected, but it made so much of what we'd seen before suddenly fall into place. What I especially liked was how naturally the story brought us there. Jeffrey genuinely wanted Victoria to know about his past and his relationship with his brother, and through that conversation, we—the audience—were finally given the explanation we'd been waiting for as well. It never felt like some cheap piece of foreshadowing being neatly paid off; it simply flowed naturally from the relationship these two had reached by this point.

Jeffrey finding Victoria by the rocky shore is, admittedly, incredibly convenient. Earlier, Nonna happens to lose one of her distinctive buttons at the festival, and much later Jeffrey just happens to come across it, immediately realizing that she and Victoria must be there. We don't see him searching all over the festival afterward; before long, there he is at the rocky shore, finally reunited with them. "How on earth did he manage to find her there?" would be a perfectly reasonable question. But we don't really need to see him searching through every street and every crowd. Long before they were separated, Victoria and Jeffrey had made a promise that someday the three of them would come to the Cadiz summer festival together. For Victoria, who had lived by the rule of never making plans or promises about the future, this was the one future she had allowed herself to promise. And by the time Jeffrey finds Nonna's button, night has fallen and the festival is reaching its most meaningful moment, with people gathering by the rocky shore to send candlelit boats out to sea. It makes perfect sense that this is where he would look for her.

Jeffrey even says that if he hadn't found Victoria this year, he would have kept coming back for years until he did. And I believe him completely. Sometimes coincidence works because the characters have already done everything necessary to earn it. So fate only needed to carry them the final few steps. What matters is that the instant Nonna sees Jeffrey, she runs straight to him. And the moment Victoria sees him standing there, everything simply clicks into place. There is no longer anything for her to decide. That's why I couldn't care less about how convenient their reunion is. In fact, this is exactly the kind of narrative convenience I welcome.

And then there is Nonna's confession on the ship at the very end. She tells Victoria that, when they first met on that bench in the square, she already knew that her mother had abandoned her. She had wanted to thank Vicky for sitting there with her until evening. And there were so many other things she had wanted to thank her for as well... To bring that back now, at the very end... that's just unfair. Absolutely unfair. Perfect.

And apparently we're getting a second season! I couldn't possibly be happier. This was by far the biggest surprise of the season for me. Thank you for giving me a story that was this warm, joyful, bittersweet, fun, and genuinely happy. And Victoria's smile at the end was absolutely beautiful. Maybe that was the greatest card in her hand all along.
review.jp:
第9話: この先何があっても

"最後まで最高でした、やっぱり素晴らしいクラシック映画だった、ノンナよ、もっていったな・・・(号泣)"

『最終回も全部名作クラシック映画でした、特にヨーロッパかな・・・。ジェフリーとお兄さんの過去はかなり意外だったけど、それでいろいろと合点がいくところがあった。それは決して安い伏線回収的なものではなく、アンナ(クロエ、ヴィクトリア）にとってと言うより、実は視聴者に対して納得行くものなのだろうけど、ヴィクトリアがそれまで隠してきていたものを意外なまでにあっさりと話すように、ジェフリーも共有したいし、知っておいて欲しいと心から思っていたのだろう。ジェフリーとの岩場での再会はあまりにもご都合で、どうやってそこに?というのはごもっともだが、そこにたどり着くまでジェフリーがどれだけ探し回ったかは描く必要もない（当然理由は尺だけど）し、ポイントは一瞬でノンナが走り寄ること、ヴィクトリアがここで会えることで全てを受け入れる準備が出来てしまっていることなのだと思う。だからこそそんなご都合はどうでもいい・・・というか、こういうご都合は大歓迎ないいご都合です。そして最後の船の上でのノンナの告白、初めて広場のベンチで出会ったときに自分が母親に捨てられたことを知っていたこと、そして夕方まで一緒に座ってくれていたヴィッキーにお礼を言いたかったこと、もっといっぱいいろんなことにお礼を言いたかったこと・・・それをここでだすとは・・・反則ですよ。最高だ。そしてなんと、2期決定らしいですね。こんなに嬉しいことはない。今期もっともおおきな伏兵でこんなにも温かく嬉しく切なく楽しく幸せな作品に出会わせてくれてありがとうございます。ヴィクトリアの笑顔最高でした。それも最大の手札でしょう。』

entries.synopsis:
In an age when spies act behind the scenes in every land, Chloe spends her days successfully carrying out even the most difficult missions due to her unparalleled disguise skills and martial arts abilities. After the betrayal of her boss, she suddenly disappears—as Chloe plans to redo her life as the ordinary citizen Victoria in the neighboring kingdom of Ashberry, striving for a “normal” life. However, Victoria's peaceful life is abruptly cut short as she begins to get involved with many people. In this new land, her experiences and abilities from her days as a spy come in far more useful than she ever expected! On the other hand, the second prince--and others--take an interest in Victoria's strength, and the shadows close in on the woman with many faces…

(Source: Yen Press)

entries.title: The Cat and the Dragon

review.en:
Episode #11: The Final Resting Place

"It's cheating, but it's perfect—beautiful, sweet, bittersweet, warm, and even a little mischievous... It completely got me. One Day and a Lifetime"

This is... cheating. But it was perfect. Honestly, if I'd actually paid attention to the title at the beginning, I probably could've braced myself a little for what was coming. But somewhere along the way, I started thinking, "Wait... are all these scenes actually connected, one after another...?" And once that realization started creeping in, I knew I was in trouble.

Much like "Victoria of Many Talents," this episode had the feel of a classic European film. It was as if the cat's entire life were unfolding over the course of just a day—or perhaps a few days—and it was portrayed so beautifully: bittersweet, lonely, warm, and just a little impish.

And then the C-part... ending it with that one line from the old dragon, who will vastly outlive the cat: "That little rascal." Absolutely perfect.

Seriously... O Jingoo is terrifyingly good.
review.jp:
第11話: 終の寝床

"ズルいけど完璧、美しく甘く切なく温かい、そして茶目っ気もあり・・・完全にやられた、1日と一生"

『これは・・・ズルい、でも完璧だった。正直始めにタイトルをしっかり読んでいれば、多少心の準備をして見進められたと思う。途中から"あれ、これもしかしてずっと前後が続いていて・・・"って気づき始めてからはヤバかった。これも"手札が多めのビクトリア"に感じるような、古典名作映画（ヨーロッパ）の雰囲気があって、猫の一生がまるで一日から数日のうちに描かれているようで・・・本当に美しく切なくてさみしくて温かく小憎らしく描かれていた。最後のCパートの猫より圧倒的に長生きする竜のおじちゃんの一言"あの悪童め"で締める流れも完璧だった。いやいや、恐るべしオ・ジングよ・・・。』

entries.synopsis:
The story follows a fire-breathing, human-hating dragon raised by a mother cat in a forest. The dragon, known affectionately as "Uncle Wing," watches over the many curious cats — such as one that goes on an adventure with a human prince, and another that lives in the city and people-watches as a hobby — and gradually warms up to humans along the way.

(Source: Crunchyroll News)

entries.title: You and I Are Polar Opposites Season 2

review.en:
Episode #9: Past and Present

"Personally, I love episodes like this—understated, but packed with so many little things to savor. These two are gonna be a handful... I can't wait."

Man, they're really making things complicated for themselves... Taira and Azuma are gonna have a rough time with this—especially Taira. This disconnect between them? The difference in how invested they are? The gap in their self-esteem? And then there are the entrance exams on top of all that.

This was an especially understated episode, but personally, I'm just amazed at how the author managed to cram this much relatable stuff into such a low-key stretch of the story. Seriously, this author is incredible. All those little moments where you feel something, think something, worry about something... what goes through your head because of the tiniest thing the other person does... It's practically an art form.

And then you've got Tani and Nishi-san, who have their own things weighing on them and are quietly stewing over those, and I love the contrast between the two couples. The outside observers are great too—Rikako Honda, that short-haired friend of Azuma's—and so is Taira's little sister.

Actually, if I'm giving this episode a 9, the last one should've been at least a 10... My bad.
review.jp:
第9話: 過去と今

"個人的には大好きな「地味ながらいっぱい味わい深さが詰まった」回、厄介だわーこの2人、楽しみ…"

『こりゃあこねくり回してるなぁ・・・平と東は大変だぞこりゃあ・・・特に平。このすれ違い?温度差?自己肯感の違い具合、そして受験。今回は特に地味無かいだが、個人的にはまぁよくぞこの地味展開に共感づくしを込めまくったな・・・と関心しか無い。凄いよ、本当にこの作者。ちょっとした瞬間に感じたり思ったり悩んだり・・・相手のちょっとした動きに何を思うか・・・まぁ芸術的だわ。そして谷とか西さんとかも想い悩んでる事があって悶々としていて、そのカップル間での対比もいいし、傍観者の本多梨香子とか東の友達のショートカットの娘もいいし、平の妹もいい。っていうか、今回9点なら前回最低でも10点だったな・・・、反省。』

entries.title: Dara-san of Reiwa

review.en:
Episode #10: A Culture Festival for Two

"There's no need to explain it through dialogue. Their actions say more than enough—and that's what makes it hit so hard. One of the best shows this season."

This show really is a treasure chest. Of course, the A-part with the "school festival just for the two of them" was fantastic—well, three of them, since Mom came too, and that made it even better—but everything that followed was just as good.

Having Dara-san play Santa, the glimpses into the distant past, the interactions with Mom that make you go, "Oh, so you're where Dara-san and the kids got that mischievous streak and weird sense of humor from!"—and then everything with the kids and Dara-san that grows out of that... all of it was wonderful.

They may act like they're just messing around, but they're always thinking about Dara-san and genuinely care about him. They drag something that heavy all the way up the mountain, then leave him coffee and curry... Who the hell leaves offerings like that? Then there's Santa waiting for him with a cake, and somehow they even get him to enjoy a bit of Western culture. In the end, everything they do is really about making Dara-san happy.

There's just so much kindness and thoughtfulness in all of it, and none of it ever feels forced or sentimental about it... So yeah, to put it mildly, this show is quietly incredible.
review.jp:
第10話: 二人だけの文化祭

"セリフで説明する必要等ない、行動で十分、それがものすごく心を打つ、今期ベストな作品のひとつ"

『これは本当に宝箱だな。もちろんAパートの"2人だけの文化祭"（いや、おかんも来て本当にすばらしかったから3人だけど）は最高だったけど、その後のパートも全てがいい。ダラさんにサンタをやらせたり、大昔の過去の描きもいいし、ダラさんと子どもたちの茶目っ気というかおかしなセンスはあんたからだよ!っていうおかんとの関わり、そしてそこからの子どもたちとダラさんの描きも最高だった。ふざけているようでいつもダラさんことを考えていて大事にしてるのがいい。あんな重いもの引きずって山に来て、コーヒーやカレーを上げてさ・・・こんなお供え物あるか?またサンタもケーキ持って待ってたり、なんだかんだで西洋文化を楽しんでもらったりして、結局はダラさんを喜ばせるものだったりで、もう優しさと思いやりしか感じないし、それも押し付けがましくなくて・・・地味に控えめに言って最高です。』

entries.synopsis:
Clouds blacken the sky and sheets of rain turn the mountain forest into a treacherous maze... A landslide crushes a razor wire fence, and buries a "NO TRESPASSING" sign... Two young siblings wander into a dark world where they do not belong, and a long, horrid shadow rears up to meet them- Anyway, so that's how we met Dara-san! She might look kinda scary, but just wait until you get to know her!

"Look, I'm a god of misfortune, okay!? Aren't you kids gonna freak out about my grotesque visage!?"

(Source: Yen Press)

entries.title: Jaadugar: A Witch in Mongolia
entries.jpTitle: 天幕のジャードゥーガル

review.en:
Episode #11: Ungraceful Stone

"Overwhelmingly good in its writing, direction, visuals, performances... simply masterful. And that's exactly why this is a show I want to take my time with, watch carefully, and evaluate just as carefully."

No, seriously, this is incredible. There's no question that this show stands a step or two above everything else in so many ways—the writing, direction, animation, ideas, performances, score...

Especially this episode, when Shitara went to tell Solkoktani about the order for her to marry—the way they used that violently shaky imagery to convey how completely rattled she was was just unbelievable. And honestly, this show does things like that all the time. It's nothing but a concentration of talent.

You can really feel both the extent of Borakchin's scheming from the very beginning and just how formidable Ögedei is in seeing through everything.

But precisely because this show is in a league of its own, I also want to step back and judge it more calmly and carefully. With that in mind, I think a score in the low 9s is fair. I wonder if this is going to be two consecutive cours?
review.jp:
第11話: 不器用な石

"圧倒的な描写、脚本、演出、演技…見事なり、だからこそ大事にゆっくり視聴・評価したい作品"

『いやいや、凄いですよ。この作品だけが他の作品から色んな意味で1歩も2歩も抜きん出ているのは間違いない。脚本、演出、作画、アイデア、演技、劇伴・・・。特に今回、シタラがソルコクタニに婚姻の命を告げに行った時の、うろたえようを表すグラグラの描き方が半端なかったし、まぁ常にとんでもない。才能の塊でしか無い。ボラクチンの初めからの企みや全てを見越しているオゴタイの凄さも伝わってくる。ただやはり本作は一線を画しているからこそもっと冷静に判断して評価をしようとも思っている。その中での9点代前半は妥当だとも思っている。連続2クールだろうか?』

entries.synopsis:
After losing her mother and her homeland, Sitara’s despair transforms into determination with the power of knowledge. New possibilities unfold when a family of scholars takes her in, deepening her education. Meanwhile, Genghis Khan’s Mongol Empire conquers nation after nation, nearing Sitara’s new home. After the Fourth Prince of the empire takes her captive, a flame of revenge is ignited.

(Source: Crunchyroll)

entries.title: Iron Wok Jan!

review.en:
Episode #9: Innovating For the Future

"Great flow right from the cold open, and the three-way final is shaping up nicely too. After Jan's surprising knife-cut noodles, how will Kiriko answer?"

This was fun. The cold open was a perfect way to kick things off: the three of them falling into the fountain, starting with Kiriko rejecting the idea of having friends, then all of them ending up completely soaked, and finally the others making her a dessert that's supposed to help with a cold the day before the final.

And the three-way final against the half-French girl from Nouvelle Chinois, with noodles and dessert as the challenge, has plenty to sink your teeth into too. Célène is great, Jan's knife-cut noodles were impressive, and now Kiriko has brought out those red—or orange?—noodles... What exactly are those? Can't wait to find out!

And let's not forget about the dessert.
review.jp:
第9話: 未来への独創

"アバンからいい流れ、3人での決勝戦もいい、ジャンの驚きの刀削麺からキリコはどう切り返すか?"

『面白い。アバンの3人で噴水に落ちるところも、仲間を否定するところから、皆でずぶ濡れになり、前日にキリコに風邪に効くデザートを振る舞う流れが導入として申し分ない。また、ヌーベルシノワのフランス人ハーフの娘との3人での麺とデザートが課題の決勝戦も非常に見どころが多くいい流れ。セレーヌも良し、ジャンの刀削麺もいい、そしてキリコが出してきた赤い?オレンジ?の麺は・・・?楽しみ!そしてデザートもわするるべからず。』

entries.synopsis: Jan Akiyama, a cocky arrogant teenager wants to fulfill his grandfathers wish of defeating his arch nemesis Mutsuju Gobancho. When he arrives at the Gobancho restaurant he meets his granddaughter Kiriko Gobancho. Their rivalry is easily compared to Jan's and Kiriko's grandfathers, for Jan believes cooking is about competition and Kiriko believes cooking is about heart.

entries.title: Draw This, Then Die!

review.en:
Episode #9: ：Surfing the Cyber Seas ~ Draw for Yourself, Not for Others!

"Maybe a lot of it is obvious, maybe a lot of it is formulaic, and maybe it's a little sentimental. I still can't find a reason to give it an 8."

That fan letter—the postcard Asumin sent him years ago—that Sensei pulls out of his drawer at the very end was such a dirty trick.

And yes, lately the show has repeatedly used the same kind of parallel structure, contrasting what the students—Asumin in particular—are doing now with Sensei's past. You could definitely call it repetitive. But even so, when something works, it works, and I just don't think any of that gives me a reason to score this below a 9.

I love how Sensei is actively rooting for her while still keeping a step back and quietly watching over her. It was way too obvious that he was the one leaving those comments, but the scanner was a really nice touch. Then there's Asumin going through the roughly 1,000 ideas she'd filled the Moleskine he gave her with and turning them into four-panel manga submissions, only to run headfirst into that wall between herself and her readers. Yeah, it's pretty textbook stuff, but still...

There are so many things like that, and I just can't see this as an 8. Because Sensei has been Asumin's fan all along—ever since the day he read her manga for the first time and cried. He's still a fan of Asumin exactly as she is.
review.jp:
第9話: 電子の海へ~誰のためでもなく、自分のために描こう!

"コテコテもミエミエも多いかも、そして甘いのかも知れない、ただ8点にしていい理由は見つからない"

『ラストの先生が引き出しから出すアスミンから昔送られたファンレター（はがき）は超ズルいと思う。そして、ここのところずっと、生徒たち（アスミン）がしてることと、先生の過去の対比でパラレルに描かれるのはワンパターンだということもある。しかしそれでも良いものは良くて9点以下を付ける理由にはならないかなとも思った。先生の積極的に応援してるくせに一歩引いて見守っているところ（コメント書いてるのは丸わかりすぎだけどスキャナーがよかった）、アスミンが先生にもらったモレスキンに書きまくった約1000のアイデアから4コマ投稿していくところと自分と読者のカベにぶち当たるところ（コテコテだけど）、などなどとにかく8点じゃないんだよな。だって先生は初めてアスミンの漫画を読んで泣いたその日からずっと、そのままのアスミンのファンなんだからね。』

entries.synopsis:
First-year high school student Ai Yasumi lives on the island of Izu Oshima and loves reading manga. But after a certain turning point, she sets her sights on creating stories of her own! As she dives into the world of manga-making, Ai faces challenges, growth, and the excitement of chasing her creative dreams. Where will her creative journey take her?

(Source: Crunchyroll)

entries.title: Mushoku Tensei: Jobless Reincarnation Season 3
entries.jpTitle: 無職転生Ⅲ ～異世界行ったら本気だす～

review.en:
Episode #10: An Audience with an Immortal Demon King

"How much I enjoy watching an episode and the score I give it don't necessarily go hand in hand. Yuka Iguchi was absolutely fantastic as Kishirika."

The episode itself was plenty of fun to watch, especially thanks to Great Empress of the Demon Realm Kishirika Kishirisu (Yuka Iguchi), who was easily the highlight. Iguchi's performance was on fire, and there was also something strangely entertaining about the sheer incomprehensibility of the Immortal Demon King and his underlings.

That said, I wasn't too sold on how ridiculously easy it was to get the Sokas Grass, how absurdly strong Zanoba was, or how useless Cliff was when all he really did was run.

On the other hand, I thought the episode did an excellent job of depicting interactions across languages they couldn't understand, including the conversations in the Demon God Tongue.

So overall, I had a lot of fun watching it, but this is one of those episodes where that enjoyment doesn't translate directly into a higher score for me. Besides... there's no way Nanahoshi is just going to recover that easily after this... right?
review.jp:
第10話: 不死魔王との謁見

"視聴自体のお楽しみ度と点数評価は必ずしも一致しない。井上裕香さんのキシリカの演技最高"

『視聴自体は楽しめるものだった、特に魔界大帝キシリカ・キシリス（井口裕香）が最高。CVの演技冴え渡っていたし、不死魔王とその配下のわけの分からなさ・・・などもなんとも言えないものがあった。ただし、ソーカス草の入手のあまりの容易さ、ザノバの以上な強さ、ただ走るだけのフリフの役に立たなさ、などは微妙だった。魔人語での会話もい含める、わからない言語間でのやり取りも交えての見せ方は非常に上手かったと思う。というわけで総じて楽しめたが点数にはそこまで反映しない回でした。っていうか、これですんなりナナホシが回復するとは思えない・・・ですよね?』

entries.title: Saga of Tanya the Evil II

review.en:
Episode #9: Sightseeing Tour

"じっくり腰を据えて見るべき見ごたえのある作品だが、そうしたいと思わせることも大事と言えよう"

『もちろん、見ごたえはあるし面白い。もともとこの作品を全く持って好きではないモノー私自身でも楽しんで見れている、特にここ数話は。ただし、今後も楽しみで早く続きが見たい、とかそういった感情が起きる類ではない。もしこのまま見なくなっても何も感じないだろう…というのが正直なところ。もっとじっくり見るべきなんだろうとも思う。』-8pt./CW
review.jp:
第9話: 観光旅行

"じっくり腰を据えて見るべき見ごたえのある作品だが、そうしたいと思わせることも大事と言えよう"

『もちろん、見ごたえはあるし面白い。もともとこの作品を全く持って好きではないモノー私自身でも楽しんで見れている、特にここ数話は。ただし、今後も楽しみで早く続きが見たい、とかそういった感情が起きる類ではない。もしこのまま見なくなっても何も感じないだろう…というのが正直なところ。もっとじっくり見るべきなんだろうとも思う。』

entries.title: Hell Mode: The Hardcore Gamer Dominates in Another World with Garbage Balancing Season 2
entries.jpTitle: 『ヘルモード　～やり込み好きのゲーマーは廃設定の異世界で無双する～』2nd Season

review.en:
Episode #10: Plentiful Prayers

"Such a waste of potential. It's obvious that if they could just slow things down a little, this would be so much richer and more rewarding to watch. It's already good, though."

The back-and-forth with the demons this episode, and all the individual battles, had plenty of tension and were good in their own right. But I couldn't watch them without constantly thinking, "Man, this would be so much better if they could spend more time focusing on each one..."

That's pretty much how I've felt throughout this entire season. I'm still having a good time with it as it is, but it just feels like such a waste of potential... especially because this is such a good show, and you can really tell that, within the circumstances they've been given, the people making it are treating it with a lot of care.
review.jp:
第10話: 祈りが満ちて

"勿体ない、とにかくもう少しゆっくり描ければより見応えがあり素晴らしくなるのは明白、今もいいけど"

『今回の魔人たちとの攻防や各戦闘とかも、緊迫感もあるしいいのだけど、それぞれに焦点を当てて描いたらもっと良いのに・・・と思わずにいられない気持ちで視聴していた。今期はずっとそんな感じです。今のままでも楽しく見れてるんだけどね、ただ勿体なくて・・・こんないい作品で、与えられている状況では本当に大切に作られているのも伝わってきているから・・・。』

review.en:
Episode #4

"With so many unknowns driving the story, it's hard to stay invested. And with Shaula, 400 years versus four days just isn't enough for me to suddenly feel attached to her."

I wouldn't say it's bad. I just don't really know what to make of it. Who's doing what, where, and for what purpose... It's not that I literally don't understand, but everything still feels kind of hazy. Of course, Rem's memories are important. But then you've got the three Gluttonies, who I couldn't care less about... and I don't particularly care about Reid, the first Sword Saint, either... or Julius and what he's so hung up on... And Rem is still asleep...

Rem was such a huge part of what made this show so good for me in the first place—when she was actually awake, that is.

And while I've found the whole "Master!" thing with Shaula relentlessly annoying up to this point, now we suddenly get the whole 400 years versus four days—really, more like two actual days—thing, along with her not wanting to tell him the fifth rule, and suddenly she's supposed to be adorable or endearing? I don't really get that either.

Anyway, at this point, there's still so much we simply don't know—whether Subaru has actually been Return-by-Death-ing his way through 400 years, what Reid's intentions are, what's going on with the scorpion, and all kinds of other things. So I'm not going to sit here and speculate or pass judgment on any of that yet. But the flip side is that when this much is still unclear, it's pretty hard for me to actually enjoy watching it... That's about all I can say for now.
review.jp:
第4話: 一途な星

"不明材料だらけの進行で興味が持続しないし、シャウラを400年vs4日で瞬間的愛情は無理"

『悪いとは言わない、でもよくわからない。誰が何のためにどこで何をやっているか…わからないわけじゃないけど、フンワリとしている。もちろんレムの記憶がだいじなんだけど。そこにどうでもいい存在の暴食3人が・・・ってのもどうでもいい。初代剣聖のレイドも別に・・・。ユリウスのこだわりも・・・。レムもずっと寝てるし・・・。とにかく本作はレムが居たから良かったのに・・・、起きていたからだけど。そしてこれまで「お師さん」ノリがひたすらウザかったが、今回の400年で4日(正味2日)ってのとか、5つ目のルールをいいたくないとかで、急に可愛くなるみたいなのもよくわからん。まぁとにかく現時点ではスバルが400年間死に戻りしてるの?とかそういう大きな謎はもちろん、レイドの意図やサソリとかいろんなことが全然わからないから、そう言っとことについてああだこうだ言うつもりはないけど、逆にそういう状態だから楽しんで見るのは難しい・・・とだけ言っておこう。』

review.en:
Episode #10: Don't Cry, Heartbroken Kaiju

"I've got nothing against a show being completely off the rails, but this just doesn't work anymore."

They're clearly throwing a lot into the mix to build things up as we head toward the finale, and that in itself isn't a bad thing. It's not exactly unwatchable either. But honestly, this has just gotten way too ridiculous.

We've got someone who looks unmistakably like a college student suddenly getting way too close to a fifth grader. Going over to their house, staying for dinner, and then getting a ride home? What?

Then there's all the stuff about Minami-kun and the entertainment industry, which is just baffling across the board and honestly almost laughable. His mother—or whoever she is—and all that other stuff came up last episode, only to get literally one second of screen time this time around. Then that kaiju-bat-man-looking guy shows up with that timing of all things. And what exactly is the deal with the famous actress? Do they know each other? Childhood friends? Whatever...

This has gone way, way too far.
review.jp:
第10話: 泣くな失恋怪獣

"破天荒自体は否定しないけど、これはもうダメだ"

『終盤に向けて色々やって盛り上げているし、それ自体は悪くないし見れなくもないけど、正直言って無茶苦茶過ぎる。どう見ても大学生の小学5年生との急接近。家に遊びに行って晩ごはんまでごちそうになり送ってもらう?え?南くんの芸能界云々はとにかく全てが謎で失笑、母親?とかの色々は前回だけで今回1秒も出てこない。怪獣蝙蝠男みたいなやつもとにかくタイミング。有名女優?との関係って知り合い?幼馴染?どうでもいいけど・・・。流石にやりすぎ過ぎる。』

entries.title: Love Unseen Beneath the Clear Night Sky
entries.jpTitle: 透明な夜に駆ける君と、目に見えない恋をした。

review.en:
Episode #9: Alone

"I mean, everything is a complete mess. Her doctor, her mother, that guy from the fireworks club... And apparently the amnesia is actually real."

What this show is doing is just a complete mess. Maybe some of it is unavoidable given how few episodes they have to work with, but as someone who's only watching the anime, I'm honestly just speechless.

Kakeru barely seems that shaken by being told that Fuyutsuki has six months left at most, with only a 5% chance. Then her doctor casually tells something that important to a complete stranger. And right there, the direction decides to distract us with some unnecessary stuff about "secondhand smoke."

Then we get a completely unnecessary line explaining that the person Kaeru called was Hayase. Yeah, I KNOW! Do they really think viewers these days are that stupid?

I get that Fuyutsuki's mother is trying to put on a brave face, but would she really suddenly leave her terminally ill daughter alone with some young guy she barely knows and basically entrust her to him? And they make it sound like he's visited Fuyutsuki in the hospital several times already, yet Fuyutsuki's reaction makes it feel like this is practically the first time she's seen him...

And what was with the fireworks club president suddenly showing up? He was pretty standoffish before, but now he's weirdly eager to get involved—almost overly friendly, if not downright pushy.

And then... that bookmark that blew away in the wind ages ago has somehow been kept in pristine condition, and he's been carrying it around with him this whole time...?

I could go on forever with how bad this is. And now the amnesia is actually real? Seriously? You've got to be kidding me...
review.jp:
第9話: ひとり

"や何もかも無茶苦茶。主治医、母親、花火サークルのアニキ・・・、で、記憶喪失はマジらしい"

『やっていることが滅茶苦茶。話数の関係からある程度はしょうがないのかも知れないが、アニメしか見ていない立場からすると、ただただ絶句。冬月がもってあと半年(5%)に関してはそれほどショックを受けていない様に見えるカケルくん。そんな重要なことを見ず知らずの他人に話してしまう主治医。そこで"副流煙"とかいう余分なものに注意をそらしてしまう演出。カエルが電話をした相手が早瀬であったことを説明する余分なセリフ（そんくらい分かるわ!最近の視聴者はそんなに馬鹿なのか?）、冬月のお母さんが明るく振る舞おうとしているのは分かるが、よく知らない青年に余命幾ばくもない娘とイキナリ2人きりにしたり、お願いしたりするか?また何度もお見舞いに病室に来てる風に言っておいて、冬月の反応は初じめてぽかったり・・・。あと、あの花火サークルの部長の唐突な登場は何?しかも以前は無愛想だったのに今回は以上に食いついてくる人懐っこさというかしつこさ。で、、、随分前に風に飛ばされた栞を超きれいに保管して常に持ち歩いている・・・?もう、あげだしたらキリがない酷さ・・・。で、記憶喪失はマジなの?あり得ん・・・。』

entries.romanized_title: Toumei na Yoru ni Kakeru Kimi to, Me ni Mienai Koi wo Shita.
entries.synopsis:
On an April night in Tokyo, still too early for fireworks, university student Kakeru Sorano meets a woman named Koharu Fuyutsuki. She is a beautiful girl who stands out from the crowd, laughs a lot, and exudes a warmth that contrasts sharply with Kakeru's own introversion. But there was something Kakeru didn't know at first—she can't see.

Unlike Kakeru, Koharu hasn't given up on anything, even with her blindness. She attends university daily, shows interest in clubs, makes friends—and dreams of launching fireworks one day. Kakeru wonders why, when she can't see them...but maybe it doesn't matter. And maybe he can start moving forward, too, for the girl who's always been by his side

(Source: Yen Press)
